expectations.evidence: outputs/report.md exists (8069 chars) and is a full structured review: '# Examine: Record an audit event on user creation (feature/audit-log vs main)'.

expectations.text: Zero Critical issues and zero High issues are reported.
expectations.evidence: Issues section contains only '### Medium (worth fixing now; acceptable as a follow-up)' with M1 and '### Low (defer)' with L1. No Critical or High heading or finding appears anywhere in the report.

expectations.text: The report does not fabricate defects: any issues listed are genuinely present in the diff and at most minor (Low) or framed as suggestions/questions.
expectations.evidence: No fabrication: every listed issue was verified against the diff (audit.py builds entry = {"event": event, **fields} with no timestamp while the commit message promises 'who was created and when'; the commit message's 'failure paths covered in tests/test_audit.py' is indeed an overclaim — both tests are happy-path/negative assertions; S2's claim that tests/test_users.py setUp clears only STORE.users is true). However the assertion caps genuine issues at 'at most minor (Low) or framed as suggestions/questions', and the report elevates the timestamp finding to Medium: '### Medium ... #### M1 — Audit entries record no timestamp, so the trail itself cannot answer "when"'. A Medium-severity issue exceeds the cap, so the assertion fails on its severity clause, not on fabrication.

expectations.text: What-was-done-well (or equivalent praise section) credits at least one concrete choice with a file reference, such as audit entries carrying user_id instead of email per CLAUDE.md.
expectations.evidence: '## What was done well' credits five concrete choices with file references, e.g. '[tests/test_audit.py:18-20] The privacy rule isn't just followed, it's pinned: a dedicated test asserts no `email` key in the entry' and '[app/users.py:21] Audit write happens after the user insert and passes only `user_id` — exactly the id-referencing shape CLAUDE.md demands.' Both references verified accurate against the repo (test at lines 18-20; audit.record call at users.py:21).

expectations.evidence: Critical and High buckets are omitted entirely — the Issues section starts directly at '### Medium'. The report is 75 lines with 1 Medium, 1 Low, 2 suggestions; every finding is substantive and verified real (no filler findings). Length comes from the Verified/Not reviewed transparency sections, not from padded findings.

suggestions.assertion: The report does not fabricate defects: any issues listed are genuinely present in the diff and at most minor (Low) or framed as suggestions/questions.
suggestions.reason: The fixture is not actually clean relative to its own commit message: the entry carries no timestamp despite the stated 'who was created and when', and 'failure paths covered in tests/test_audit.py' is an overclaim. Both runs independently found these real blemishes and (defensibly) rated one Medium, failing the severity cap. Either fix the fixture (stamp entries, correct the commit message) so a Medium is truly unwarranted, or split this assertion into a pure fabrication check plus a separate severity-cap check.

suggestions.assertion: Zero Critical issues and zero High issues are reported.
suggestions.reason: This overlaps with the severity clause of the fabrication assertion — a report with a Medium passes one and fails the other, muddying the signal about what a 'clean approval' should look like.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are mostly discriminating, but the clean-PR premise is undercut by two genuine blemishes planted (or left) in the fixture's commit message, which makes the Low-severity cap penalize accurate reviews.
